title: How to Find Companies by Funding Round Type
summary: Find companies by funding round with the PredictLeads Discover endpoint: filter by seed, Series A, B and beyond, with investors and amounts.
body_text: To find companies that just raised, call the PredictLeads Discover Financing Events endpoint and filter by normalized financing type. The types cover the full range from pre-seed through late-stage series and their bridges. Live counts right now: 18,129 Seed rounds , 15,254 Series A rounds, and 8,101 Series B rounds. Fresh capital means budget and urgency. A newly funded company is hiring, buying tools, and building process, which makes funding one of the highest-intent signals a GTM team or agency can act on. Table of Contents Toggle What funding types can you filter by? Financing types are normalized, so messy source labels resolve to clean values you can query. A snapshot of current volumes by stage: Normalized type Stage Events now seed Seed 18,129 series_a Series A 15,254 series_b Series B 8,101 Beyond these, the normalized set includes pre-seed, later series through series_j, and plus-rounds, extensions, and bridges such as series_a_plus and series_b1. A query for a type returns those rounds no matter how each source phrased it. How do you find recently funded companies? Pass one or more financing types, and optionally a company location. Through the MCP server: Using the PredictLeads MCP server, find companies that raised a Series B. Return company name, domain, round amount, and the investors. The equivalent endpoint call: financing_events(financing_types_normalized: ["series_b"], company_location: "United States") What does a financing event include? Each event is detailed enough to prioritize and personalize: the amount as reported and an amount_normalized value the financing_type and its normalized form effective_date and found_at the investors involved the source articles behind the round How do you add investor context and expand the list? The investors on each round connect to the Portfolio Companies dataset, so you can move from one funded company to the rest of an investor’s portfolio. You can also take a funded company and pull lookalikes to find similar companies that may raise next. The strongest play is the double signal. Combine a funding filter with a hiring or technology filter to find companies that just raised and are already spending, for example funded and hiring: company_job_openings(company_id_or_domain: "example.com", onet_codes: "15-2051.00") How do GTM teams and agencies use this? Time the outreach. Reach out while the budget is fresh and vendor decisions are still open. Prioritize by round. Sort by stage and amount to focus on companies with the means to buy. Agency lists. Build “just raised” lists for clients that sell into funded startups, refreshed as new rounds land. PredictLeads collects this funding data as a first-party dataset, so you are working from the source rather than a resold database. How do you prioritize funded companies? A raise is a signal, but not all raises are equal for your pipeline. Three attributes help you sort: Amount. The normalized amount tells you how much budget just landed, which correlates with how much a company can spend. Recency. The effective date shows how fresh the round is; the first few months after a raise are when new tools get bought. Stage fit. A seed company and a Series D company buy differently, so match the stage to the price point and motion your product fits. What about bridge and extension rounds? The normalized types include bridges and extensions such as series_a_plus and series_b1. These often signal a company raising to reach the next milestone, which can mean tighter budgets but clearer priorities. Filtering them in or out lets you separate momentum raises from stopgap ones. Frequently Asked Questions How do I find companies that recently raised funding? Call the Discover Financing Events endpoint and filter by normalized financing type, such as seed or series_b. It returns companies with matching rounds, ordered by update date. What funding round types can I filter by? Normalized types range from pre-seed and seed through late-stage series and their bridges and extensions, so source labels resolve to clean, queryable values. Does the data include investors and amounts? Yes. Each financing event includes the round amount, the normalized type, source articles, and the investors involved. How do I combine funding with other signals? Add a hiring or technology filter to the funded list. Companies that just raised and are already hiring or running your target stack are the highest-intent accounts. title: 64x Bio Raises $55 Million Series A Financing to Advance Cell Line Engineering Platform for Gene Therapy Manufacturing
body_text: Multibillion-dollar gene therapy market facing critical manufacturing bottleneck that limits reach of lifesaving therapies to patients VectorSelect™ platform has the potential to revolutionize the economics and accessibility of gene therapy. ‍ SAN FRANCISCO – 64x Bio , a synthetic biology company, today announced the close of a $55 million Series A financing round to fund the expansion of its VectorSelect™ platform, a novel cell line engineering technology which has the potential to revolutionize the economics and accessibility of gene therapy. ‍ The Series A financing was led by Lifeforce Capital, with significant participation from Northpond Ventures, individual investor Michael Chambers (co-founder and former CEO of Aldevron), Future Ventures, and insider First Round Capital. Chris Gibson (co-founder and CEO of Recursion), Alix Ventures, as well as previous investors, Fifty Years, SV Angel, BoxGroup, and Refactor Capital, also participated in the oversubscribed round. ‍ The funding will advance 64x’s cell line engineering platform VectorSelect™ to design improved cell lines for a wide range of gene therapies. 64x will also use the proceeds to dramatically grow its employee base and partnership efforts with leading gene therapy companies, through the expansion of additional intellectual property, operations, and business development infrastructure. ‍ “This Series A financing will allow us to take VectorSelect™ to the next level and grow our business infrastructure to establish more partnerships,” said Alexis “Lex” Rovner, PhD, CEO & co-founder, 64x Bio. “With the support of our incredible investors and scientific team, we aim to become the leading developer of vector manufacturing cell lines, to revolutionize the economics of gene therapy and the reach of these lifesaving medicines to patients.” ‍ “Viral vectors, engineered viruses that deliver a genetic payload to cells, are a critical component of many biologic drugs. Current vector manufacturing cell lines suffer from poor yield and quality, limiting the scale and impact of biologics drug development. This limitation is a major bottleneck for the gene therapy field, which relies heavily on vectors,” said Sander Duncan, General Partner at Lifeforce Capital, who joins 64x’s Board of Directors. “64x’s technology platform VectorSelect™ has the potential to reduce cost and increase manufacturing capacity by orders of magnitude,” he added. ‍ With current cell lines, vector manufacturing carries tremendous cost and in-house manufacturing capacity is exceeded for even the smallest disease populations. For gene therapy to deliver on its potential to address widespread diseases, capacity would need to increase by six orders of magnitude in many cases. “Contract manufacturers are facing multi-year waitlists due to increasing demand from the growing market, so simply outsourcing the process is not a solution. Combined with prohibitively high manufacturing costs, this means that many gene therapies cannot be manufactured today, and 64x directly addresses this challenge,” said Michael Chambers. ‍ “The industry has poured billions of dollars into the expansion of vector manufacturing facilities in recent years. However, the problem is more fundamental than physical infrastructure. This is a genetics problem and the solutions are going to be in tailoring how a cell interacts with the viral components,” said George Church, PhD, co-founder of 64x Bio, Professor of Genetics at Harvard Medical School, and founding Core Faculty member at the Wyss Institute at Harvard University. “Until now, genetic tailoring of manufacturing cells has failed to deliver. Overcoming the cellular barriers to viral production will require many cellular mutations in combination, which means testing potentially trillions of mutant cells. Existing cell line engineering and screening technologies have not been up to the challenge,” he added. ‍ VectorSelect™ uniquely allows 64x to map millions of unique cellular genotypes to their individual vector production phenotypes. In this way, the technology enables high-throughput data generation from massively multiplexed experiments on millions of candidate cell lines simultaneously. 64x then applies computational tools to its growing CellMap™ database of proprietary mutant data to filter trillions of possible solutions into millions of screenable genetic combinations, further increasing the speed and efficacy of cell line development. Together, this enables discovery of cell lines with otherwise unattainable and radically improved productivities. The company is currently focused on cell and gene therapy and plans to expand to other markets in the future. ‍ About 64x Bio ‍ Using novel high throughput genome engineering and screening technologies in a design loop with computational tools, 64x Bio is developing new ways of generating highly optimized and otherwise unattainable cell lines for the manufacturing of viral vectors, with a specific focus on those used for cell and gene therapies. The novel approach developed by founders at Harvard Medical School and the Wyss Institute at Harvard University promises to bring more cell and gene therapies to patients. The company is headquartered in San Francisco, CA. For more information, visit www.64xbio.com . Follow us on Twitter @64xbio. ‍ Contacts Media: Kimberly Ha KKH Advisors 917-291-5744 kimberly.ha@kkhadvisors.com ‍

title: Is It Time to Safely Return to In-Person Events?
body_text: Three Considerations: Over the past year and a half, marketing events (and all other in-person activities) were shifted en masse from face-to-face to virtual. Unfortunately, this was not out of choice but out of necessity to keep people safe and healthy during a global pandemic. In-person marketing events just couldn’t be managed safely enough to warrant meeting, especially when virtual options were so readily available. Today, however, we are finally (fingers crossed!) on the other side of this pause to everyday life. Widespread vaccine distribution has ensured that everyone in the U.S. that wants to get vaccinated has the option and ability to receive a vaccine. In addition, over the last nineteen months, society has become more aware and conscious of the health risks posed by in-person contact and how to prevent these risks. Here are some points to consider when deciding whether or not it is safe for your team to return to in-person events: — The type of event you’re attending or hosting All events are not created equal, especially when it comes to in-person health and safety measures. If you’re concerned about safety at your upcoming events, think about the type of event you’re hosting or attending. A giant conference in an event center basement is different from an intimate outdoor happy hour at a local restaurant. Ask your attendees what they’re comfortable with and adjust your itinerary to meet their comfort level. — Health & safety precautions in place We haven’t spent the last two years practicing social distancing and disinfecting for nothing, and these precautions can roll over into your event marketing strategy. Asking attendees to wear masks, giving out hand sanitizer as booth swag, and strategically setting up demo stations to take social distancing into account are all ways you can put health and safety precautions in place while still embracing in-person engagement. — Virtual options still available Even if you’re running headfirst towards in-person events, keep in mind that virtual options are still available. It has become the norm to provide a virtual option for any in-person event, creating a hybrid, multi-channel event strategy. Your attendees will appreciate the option and attention to their safety, and your marketing team can experiment with new and exciting marketing campaigns and ideas. ‍ Is your team returning to in-person events this year? Like almost everyone else in the world, event marketing teams are clamoring to get back there and do what they do best – engage directly with people. Whether your team is returning to an entirely in-person schedule this year or if you’re gearing up for more hybrid events, the Circa event marketing platform can help make the transition easier.

title: AI Accounting Software: 7 Best in July 2026
summary: Explore 7 AI accounting software tools in July 2026 that automate reconciliations and reduce close time by 30-50% for accounting firms and finance teams.
body_text: Closing the books without spending three full days on bank reconciliations and variance writeups is rare for firms managing more than a handful of clients. That manual work eats up the majority of the close cycle before the actual review begins. Per APQC benchmarking data , the median finance team takes 6.4 days to complete the monthly close. The difference between ai accounting software that assists and software that executes is where firms are finding real capacity gains. The tools that post journal entries and run reconciliations automatically are saving teams 30 to 50 percent of their close time per engagement. TLDR: AI accounting software splits between tools that flag issues and tools that execute work like reconciliations and journal entries directly. Most tools cover transaction categorization and anomaly detection, but only a few handle full workflow automation across the close. Firms using Double report 30 to 50 percent time savings per close through AI-driven reconciliation and flux analysis. Tools built for single-entity corporate closes create friction for accounting firms managing multi-client portfolios. Double automates the close for accounting firms with two-way sync to QuickBooks Online and Xero, per-client pricing, and a built-in client portal. What is AI Accounting Software? AI accounting software refers to tools that use AI to automate, analyze, or assist with financial recordkeeping, reporting, and related workflows. The category spans a wide range of capabilities, from basic automation that categorizes transactions to more advanced systems that flag anomalies, draft variance explanations, or close the books with minimal human input. Industry research indicates that 50 percent of accounting teams cite productivity improvements as the primary benefit, with 39 percent reporting faster financial close and reconciliation in particular. Some AI accounting software sits in the background, surfacing suggestions or flagging items for review. Others take a more active role, running reconciliations, preparing journal entries, and generating financial reports without waiting for someone to initiate each step. Tools that execute work directly eliminate more manual tasks than tools that only flag issues for review. Automated transaction categorization that learns from historical patterns and applies rules across connected accounts, reducing the manual work of coding entries one by one. Anomaly detection that monitors account balances and transaction data continuously, surfacing items that fall outside expected ranges before they become reporting errors. AI-assisted reporting that drafts financial statements, variance commentary, and close summaries based on live data without requiring an analyst to build them from scratch each period. Workflow automation that moves tasks through a defined close sequence, assigns owners, tracks status, and flags blockers without relying on spreadsheets or email threads to coordinate the work. Most tools in this roundup cover at least two or three of these areas. The best ones cover all four. How We Assessed AI Accounting Software Each tool in this roundup was assessed across five criteria, drawing from publicly available product documentation, vendor websites, and verified third-party sources. No vendor received advance review of this content. Execution capability: whether AI posts transactions directly to the ledger or generates output that still requires a manual posting step Integration depth: native two-way sync with QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, or NetSuite AI surface area: how broadly AI applies across bank feeds, journal entries, reconciliations, and accruals Pricing transparency: whether costs are clearly published and scale predictably as workload grows Workflow consolidation: whether the tool replaces point solutions or adds another layer to an existing stack Best Overall AI Accounting Software: Double Double is purpose-built for accounting firms managing multi-client month-end closes, and it goes well beyond task tracking. Where most tools hand you a checklist, Double does the actual work: pulling in transaction data, running reconciliations, drafting variance explanations, and posting journal entries automatically. Core Capabilities Two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and Xero means the close stays connected to live client data without manual exports or copy-paste workflows. AI flux analysis automatically drafts variance explanations at the vendor and transaction level across the P&L and Balance Sheet, with configurable materiality thresholds so reviewers start from conclusions instead of raw numbers. Reconciliations run inside the close workflow itself, with AI matching transactions and flagging exceptions for human review instead of handing accountants a blank spreadsheet. The client portal handles document requests, status updates, and approvals in one place, cutting the back-and-forth that typically drags out the final days of any close. Pricing Double charges per connected client with no user fees and no seat limits. Firms using Double report saving 30 to 50 percent of close time per engagement, which compounds quickly across a full client portfolio. Who It's For Double fits accounting firms where tax prep, audit, and advisory all run simultaneously and the close needs to move across multiple client entities without falling apart at the seams. If your team is still manually exporting reports, chasing client documents over email, or rebuilding variance stories from scratch each month, Double is built for that exact problem. Basis Basis is AI accounting software built for accounting firms, and it sits in a different category from most tools on this list. Where others focus on bookkeeping automation or close management, Basis targets the full client accounting workflow, from onboarding to ongoing monthly work. The core of Basis is its AI categorization engine. It learns from your firm's coding history and applies that knowledge across clients, reducing the manual review cycle that burns hours every month. Core Capabilities Transaction categorization that adapts to firm-specific rules, not generic chart-of-accounts logic Client request management built into the workflow so document collection doesn't happen over email Month-end checklists with task ownership and status tracking across your client portfolio A client-facing portal where clients can respond to questions and upload documents directly Where Basis Fits Best Basis works well for firms doing high-volume bookkeeping across many small business clients. The categorization accuracy improves over time, which means the tool gets more useful the longer a firm uses it. That said, Basis is less suited for firms whose primary work is audit, tax, or advisory, since the product is built around the transactional bookkeeping workflow instead of close integrity or financial reporting. Pricing is not publicly listed, so firms will need to request a demo to get a quote. Dext Dext sits in the document capture and receipt management space, focusing on pulling financial data out of paper and digital documents before it reaches your accounting software. It uses AI to extract data from receipts, invoices, and bank statements, then pushes that structured data into connected tools like QuickBooks Online and Xero. Strengths Optical character recognition accuracy has improved with AI, making it reliable for high-volume receipt capture across clients who submit documents in inconsistent formats. The supplier rules engine learns from past transactions and auto-categorizes line items, reducing repetitive manual coding work for bookkeepers handling recurring vendors. Mobile capture through the Dext app lets clients photograph receipts on the go, cutting down on the end-of-month document chase that slows reconciliation. Where Dext Stops Dext handles the intake layer well, but the workflow ends at data extraction. There is no close management, no reconciliation execution, and no month-end task coordination built in. For accounting firms looking for AI accounting software that moves beyond document capture into actual close work, Dext solves one part of a larger problem. Dext works best for firms or bookkeepers managing high document volumes who need a reliable front-end capture tool to feed their existing accounting software. FloQast FloQast has a large and active user base, particularly among mid-market corporate accounting departments. Many teams know the name, and for good reason: it has invested heavily in close management workflows, reconciliation tracking, and audit-trail documentation. For accounting firms managing multi-client portfolios, the limitation worth noting is structural. FloQast was built for internal corporate finance teams managing a single entity, and its architecture reflects that. Firms running concurrent client closes hit friction quickly, since the tool assumes one set of books instead of a portfolio of clients with separate close cycles. Pricing also skews toward enterprise budgets, with user-based fees and multi-year commitments that can strain smaller firms considering cost per engagement. Numeric Numeric was built for corporate finance teams managing a single entity's close, not for accounting firms running multi-client portfolios. That design choice works well in its intended context, but it creates real friction for firms that need to manage closes across dozens of clients simultaneously. The core limitation worth noting is structural. Numeric assumes one set of books, one close workflow, one team. Accounting firms that try to scale across clients hit that wall quickly. Flux analysis and variance explanations are genuinely polished, giving finance teams clear narrative context for period-over-period swings without manual writeups. The reconciliation workflow is clean and well-designed for controllers who live inside a single entity's chart of accounts day to day. Its AI features are built around a corporate close cadence, which suits in-house finance teams with predictable monthly rhythms. For accounting firms, the fit gap shows up fast. There is no multi-client workspace, no client-facing portal, and no way to manage concurrent closes across separate entities from a single view. Each client effectively requires its own isolated workflow, which eliminates the time savings firms depend on when running five, ten, or fifty closes in parallel. Numeric is a capable close tool for the audience it was designed for. For accounting firms managing client portfolios, that audience is not you. Ramp Stack Ramp Stack is Ramp's named AI product for accounting firms, announced in June 2026. It is worth including here because some firms already use Ramp for expense management and want to understand where the close management capabilities begin and end. Ramp Stack offers Skills-based AI, reconciliation workpapers, flux analysis, and accrual roll-forwards. The native data advantage is real: if your clients run Ramp cards, the transaction data flows in without manual imports or CSV wrangling. The structural limitation worth noting is architectural. For accounting firms managing multi-client portfolios, AI output that lands in spreadsheets, the absence of a client portal, and reporting anchored to a single entity create friction at scale. Teams running a single entity's books will not hit the same wall. Xenett Xenett is an AI-powered bookkeeping review tool designed for accounting firms. Where most close tools focus on task tracking or document storage, Xenett focuses on a narrower problem: catching errors in your books before they reach the client. The core workflow runs on automated error detection. Xenett scans your QuickBooks Online or Xero file and flags anomalies like duplicate transactions, misclassified entries, unusual balances, and accounts that haven't moved in months. You get a ranked list of issues to review instead of hunting through the ledger manually. Core Capabilities Automated error and anomaly detection across the chart of accounts, surfacing duplicates, miscoded entries, and stale balances without manual scanning. A client collaboration layer that lets you send questions directly to clients inside the tool, with responses tied to the specific transaction in question. Review checklists that assign sign-off steps to team members, so nothing gets approved without the right eyes on it. Flux analysis that compares period-over-period balances and flags variances worth investigating. Where It Fits and Where It Stops Xenett is well-suited for firms that want a faster bookkeeping review process and a cleaner handoff to advisory or tax. The error detection genuinely reduces the time spent hunting for problems in a messy file. The limitation worth noting is scope. Xenett is a review tool, not a close management tool. It catches what's wrong after the books are already in progress, but it doesn't own the workflow that gets you there. Firms managing complex multi-client closes with parallel workstreams will likely need something that goes deeper into close orchestration. Feature Comparison Table of AI Accounting Software Tool Best For AI Capabilities Key Integrations Starting Price Double Accounting firms and mid-market finance teams running multi-client or multi-entity closes AI-driven reconciliation, automated journal entries, flux analysis, accrual and prepaid automation QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite Per-client pricing for firms; flat annual rate for corporate finance teams Basis Accounting firms doing high-volume bookkeeping across many small business clients AI transaction categorization that learns from firm-specific coding history, client request management QuickBooks Online, Xero Custom pricing Dext Firms or bookkeepers managing high document volumes who need reliable front-end capture OCR data extraction from receipts and invoices, supplier rules engine, automated line item categorization QuickBooks Online, Xero Custom pricing FloQast Mid-market corporate accounting departments managing a single entity Close management workflows, reconciliation tracking, audit-trail documentation NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks Online Custom pricing Numeric Corporate finance teams managing a single entity's close Flux analysis, variance explanations, reconciliation workflows NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks Online Custom pricing Ramp Stack Firms whose clients already use Ramp cards for expense management Skills-based AI, reconciliation workpapers, flux analysis, accrual roll-forwards Ramp, QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite Custom pricing Xenett Firms that want a faster bookkeeping review process and cleaner handoff to advisory or tax Automated error and anomaly detection, duplicate transaction flagging, flux analysis, review checklists QuickBooks Online, Xero Custom pricing Price alone tells an incomplete story. Tools like Sage Intacct and NetSuite carry custom enterprise pricing that scales with modules and users, so the number you see at the end of a demo can look very different from what gets published. On the AI side, the gap between tools that apply AI to individual transactions versus tools that apply it across the full close workflow is where the real difference in time savings shows up. Why Double is the Best AI Accounting Software Double serves two distinct workflows with the same execution-first AI engine: accounting firms managing month-end closes across multiple clients, and corporate finance teams running the close for their own company. Most tools in this category are built for one audience. Double covers both with a direct two-way connection to the ledger. For accounting firms, that means two-way sync with QuickBooks Online and Xero. For corporate finance teams, it means the same direct connection to your ERP system. Either way, transactions pulled from the general ledger are automatically matched, categorized, and verified against bank feeds without manual data entry. Firms using Double report saving 30 to 50 percent of close time per engagement. AI That Does the Work Instead of Flagging It Most AI accounting tools surface anomalies and then hand the problem back to you. Double's AI acts on the data. It auto-categorizes transactions, drafts journal entries, and runs flux analysis with configurable materiality thresholds so reviewers start on conclusions, not raw data. Communication Built Into the Close Accounting firms get a built-in client portal where document requests, client responses, and supporting files live inside the same workspace as the close. When a client uploads a receipt or answers a question, it lands directly in the relevant task. Corporate finance teams get a stakeholder collaboration layer that lets department heads and budget owners review expenses, submit variance explanations, and approve allocations without requiring access to the accounting system. Either way, the back-and-forth that typically drags out the final days of the close stays inside the same workspace where the work happens. Close Management Across Clients and Entities Accounting firms get a practice-wide view where each client engagement has its own close workspace, with status visible across every engagement from a single view. Corporate finance teams get multi-entity close support, with subsidiary filtering across P&L, Balance Sheet, and transaction reports, and the ability to manage closes across multiple legal entities from one workspace. Reviewers can move between clients or entities, flag blockers, and track progress without switching tools or rebuilding context. Pricing Designed for Your Model Accounting firms pay per connected client, with tiers at $10, $25, or $50 per client per month depending on close complexity, and no user fees or per-seat costs. The cost scales with actual work as a firm grows its client base. Corporate finance teams pay a straightforward flat annual rate, with full team access and no per-user charges. Both models are built around how each audience actually works. Final Thoughts on AI Accounting Tools Most AI accounting software still hands the work back to you after surfacing an issue. The tools that genuinely reduce close time are the ones that execute reconciliations, post journal entries, and generate variance explanations without stopping for approval at each step. Firms managing concurrent client closes need software that runs the workflow instead of only tracking it. Book a demo if you want to see what execution-first AI looks like in practice.

title: StandardAero Inducts First SunExpress CFM LEAP-1B Engine Under New Agreement
summary: Milestone Follows Airline’s Selection of StandardAero as a LEAP MRO Provider SCOTTSDALE, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- StandardAero, Inc.…...
body_text: StandardAero Inducts First SunExpress CFM LEAP-1B Engine Under New Agreement July 16, 2026 8:00 am EDT Download as PDF Milestone Follows Airline’s Selection of StandardAero as a LEAP MRO Provider SCOTTSDALE, Ariz.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- StandardAero, Inc. (NYSE: SARO), a leading independent pure-play provider of aerospace engine aftermarket services including engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) and engine component repair, has recently inducted a CFM International LEAP-1B engine for SunExpress , a joint venture of Turkish Airlines and Lufthansa. The LEAP-1B powers SunExpress’ fleet of new generation Boeing 737-8 aircraft. Induction of this initial engine follows SunExpress’ selection of StandardAero as a LEAP-1B MRO provider, giving the airline access to the wide range of LEAP service offerings provided by StandardAero from its facility in San Antonio, TX. These services include performance restoration shop visits (PRSVs), quick-turn shop visits (QTSVs), component repairs and short-term engine leases. Commenting on the partnership, Cemil Sayar, Operations Director at SunExpress, said: “At SunExpress, we place great importance on working with trusted partners who support our commitment to safe, reliable and efficient operations. We are pleased to collaborate with StandardAero on LEAP-1B engine services and look forward to building a strong and long-term partnership together.” Commenting on the announcement for StandardAero, Guillaume Limouzy, Sales Director – Europe, Middle East & Africa (EMEA), said: “StandardAero is delighted to add SunExpress, one of Europe’s best known and highest rated leisure airlines, to our list of CFM LEAP MRO customers. We look forward to establishing ourselves as a trusted partner to SunExpress, and to providing the airline with LEAP-1B MRO services for many years to come.” StandardAero supports the LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B engine family from its 810,000 sq. ft. facility in San Antonio as a CFM LEAP Premier MRO provider, having signed the first non-airline CFM Branded Service Agreement (CBSA) in the Americas for the LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B in March 2023. The company has been providing LEAP quick-turn shop visit (QTSV) services to operators since March 2024, and completed correlation of its first test cell for the LEAP in November 2024, paving the way for PRSV inductions. As of July 2026, StandardAero has completed multiple LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B PRSV workscopes, and continues to ramp-up its capacity. In addition to establishing MRO capability for the LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B at its San Antonio facility, StandardAero is also industrializing new engine component repairs for the LEAP family through its Component Repair Services (CRS) team’s network of locations, and its Repair Development Center of Excellence. To date, StandardAero’s CRS team has industrialized more than 475 component repairs for the LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B. StandardAero also continues to grow its team of LEAP technicians through its in-house Aviation Mechanic Training Program, located at its San Antonio site’s Training Academy. Founded in Antalya as a joint venture of Turkish Airlines and Lufthansa, SunExpress acts as a tourism ambassador between Turkey and Europe with over 35 years of experience and leisure airline expertise. Operating flights to 250 routes across 37 countries, SunExpress carries nearly 16 million passengers annually with over 4,500 employees based in Antalya, Frankfurt, Izmir, Ankara and Dalaman. For more information, please visit www.sunexpress.com . A 50/50 joint venture between GE Aerospace and Safran Aircraft Engines , CFM International has redefined international cooperation and helped change the course of commercial aviation since its founding in 1974. Today, CFM is the world's leading supplier of commercial aircraft engines with a product line that sets the industry standard for efficiency, reliability, durability, and optimized cost of ownership. CFM International produces the LEAP family of engines and supports LEAP and CFM56 fleets for operators worldwide. See www.cfmaeroengines.com . StandardAero (stand #4330) will be showcasing its capabilities at the Farnborough International Airshow 2026, taking place July 20 – 24 at the Farnborough International Exhibition & Conference Centre in Hampshire, United Kingdom. StandardAero is a leading independent pure-play provider of aerospace engine aftermarket services for fixed- and rotary-wing aircraft, serving the commercial, military and business aviation end markets. StandardAero provides a comprehensive suite of critical, value-added aftermarket solutions, including engine maintenance, repair and overhaul, engine component repair, on-wing and field service support, asset management and engineering solutions. StandardAero is an NYSE listed company under the ticker symbol SARO. For more information about StandardAero, go to www.standardaero.com . title: Battery precision is the foundation of AI power stability
summary: As GPU clusters ramp up and down in milliseconds, the gap between stable operations and costly infrastructure failure comes down to one thing: how accurately your battery system knows its own state.
body_text: Artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure runs fast. Power management for AI needs to be precise, stable, and reliable. Modern AI workloads — from large language model (LLM) training to real-time inference — generate rapid, large-burst power patterns that cycle between idle and peak draw in fractions of a second. These fluctuations propagate upstream and stress generators, transformers, switchgear, and utility connections. For years, operators have worked around this challenge with familiar but imperfect tools: oversizing upstream infrastructure to absorb worst-case spikes, imposing software-based power caps on graphics processing unit (GPU) clusters to artificially limit peak draw, or managing generator instability reactively through operations teams. These approaches reduce exposure but don’t eliminate it. They also come at a cost: higher capital expenditure (CapEx), reduced compute utilization, and longer job completion times. Input power smoothing (IPS): Manage and prevent consequences Input power smoothing (IPS) uses integrated lithium battery cabinets working in tight coordination with Vertiv™ power converters to act as an active energy buffer between AI loads and upstream power sources. When load fluctuations stay within UPS capacity, the battery stays out of the loop entirely. Upstream sources see a stable, controlled demand profile. When load spikes exceed capacity, the battery steps in as a short-duration energy source, absorbing the volatility before it reaches the grid. State of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH) accuracy IPS is only as reliable as the data driving these collective patterns and insights. At the heart of every IPS decision is the battery management system (BMS). Specifically, two metrics calculating millions of data points with precision: State of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH). When SOC and SOH are communicated accurately, the uninterruptible power supply (UPS) can make real-time decisions to balance IPS performance with backup protection. In this research, discover: Why AI load volatility increases dependence on accurate battery state reporting What accurate and precise reporting enables across near-, medium-, and long-term operations How engineered integration between the battery cabinet and UPS makes IPS effective for modern AI load profiles Accurate SOC protects uptime. Accurate SOH protects the lifecycle. Engineered integration makes it work. Download the white paper to understand why precision battery management is a strategic advantage for AI infrastructure at scale.

title: AWS Parallel Computing Service now supports node lifecycle actions
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS Parallel Computing Service now supports node lifecycle actions
body_text: Today, AWS announces the general availability of node lifecycle actions in AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS). With node lifecycle actions, you can run custom scripts automatically at defined points in a compute node's lifecycle. You can use them to prepare your nodes for work. For example, you can mount shared storage, join a directory service, install software, or set up monitoring. You define node lifecycle actions in your PCS compute node group configuration when you create or update the group, and you can reuse the same script across multiple compute node groups and clusters. For each script, you set its location as an Amazon S3 or HTTPS URI, the arguments to pass, which lifecycle stage it runs in, whether it re-runs on reboot, and its error-handling behavior. AWS PCS writes the output to a dedicated log file, giving you visibility into what ran. AWS PCS is a managed service that simplifies running and scaling high performance computing (HPC) workloads on AWS using Slurm. You can build complete, elastic environments that integrate compute, storage, networking, and visualization tools, and the service manages cluster updates and provides built-in observability. Node lifecycle actions are available in all AWS Regions that support AWS PCS. To learn more, see the AWS PCS User Guide .
